before: announced as 100–150 miles long, no obvious/clear route yet; capacity noted as scalable to 2 bcf/d
after: Energy Transfer held a non-binding open season in late 2024 for a line of 100 to 150 miles from the Carthage, Texas, area, with 1 billion cubic feet per day of capacity that could grow past 2 billion. A binding open season ran from October 28 to November 25, 2026 for a redesigned line of about 215 miles from Richland Parish, Louisiana, to the George County, Mississippi, area. The pipe will be 36-inch or 42-inch, and service is expected on or before March 1, 2030. Anchor shippers have signed binding commitments. As of November 2026 there was no final investment decision and no FERC filing. The binding notice gives no capacity, so the capacity is still the 2024 figure. No route map found.
